description: We wil be building a gamified space education platform. It puts young learners in virtual space suits to solve scientific puzzles and tackle critical cosmic missions. By turning theory into an immersive STEM adventure, it delivers a highly engaging, interactive, and impactful learning experience for Students
summary: What if saving a space mission depended on listening to your teammates? We have developed an interactive game for children aged 7–12, where the classroom becomes a space mission control centre. Students are divided into four teams and face challenges inspired by real NASA missions and research. Each team has its own tablet, with different information and tools. In some rounds, the teams need to share what they have discovered and discuss their ideas to make a decision together. In others, they compete to find the best solution. What makes the game different is that their decisions have visible consequences within the game. They can see the results of their actions on the main class screen, understand their mistakes and think about how to improve. Our goal is to bring space science closer to children by letting them experience it, rather than just study it. But we also want to go further: we want children to ask questions, defend their ideas and learn to listen to others. We want them to realise that they won't always be right, and that listening to their teammates and bringing different ideas together can lead to better results.
details:
What have we developed?

We have developed an interactive classroom game where children become space explorers and face challenges inspired by real NASA missions.

The game connects a main classroom screen with four team devices. Students investigate, share information or compete to find the best solution. At the end, they see the consequences of their choices on the main screen. They also discover the science behind the challenge using real NASA data, and sometimes have the chance to improve their strategies.

Children can also play individually in solo mode.

What benefits does it have? 

We believe learning is not just about memorizing information, but also about connecting with others and listening to different perspectives. Our game encourages teamwork, communication and inclusion. Every child has something to contribute, even if they don't always agree with their teammates.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Education is still often based on memorizing information and finding the right answer. But in real life, we also need to communicate, think critically and work with others. We want children to feel included and to become more confident sharing their ideas, asking questions and understanding that sometimes there isn't just one correct solution.

How is your project creative?

We wanted to turn a space game, something children would normally play at home, into an educational tool that makes learning more fun and brings classmates together. Children face challenges inspired by real NASA missions and situations astronauts could experience. They make their own decisions, feel part of the mission and discover how science can help them solve real problems.

What factors did your team consider?

We considered the different ages and knowledge levels of children, making the challenges simple enough to understand but still exciting. Scientific accuracy was also important to us. We used real NASA research and data, simplifying some information to make it easier for children to understand, while keeping the science behind it accurate.
